newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain one-year bill yields seen setting record low.
newsitem.headline: Spain one-year bill yields seen setting record low.

text.p: Spanish Treasury one-year bill yields should set a record low at an auction on Wednesday, after the previous sale at 6.48 percent on November 13, dealers said.
The bills were trading on Tuesday morning on the grey market at around 5.95/6.05 percent and the expectation was that they would be allotted at around 6.00 percent.
After lower-than-expected October inflation data, Spanish short-term interest rates declined sharply in anticipation of a new official rate cut by the Bank of Spain before year end.
Analysts were eyeing the November CPI data due on December 13, which, if it confirmed a lowering trend, could trigger a 25 basis point cut.
"In the last two weeks we saw a sharp drop in the interbank deposits' yields and in the T-bills," a dealer said.
Traders said market rates were discounting even more than that in anticipation of further declines in interest rates if Spain were to join European Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.
"We are aiming at lower rates not only because of inflation but also because of Euro convergence which should bring interest rates lower," a dealer said.
The expectations of further reductions in market rates and heavy demand by investment trusts should push up the total amount of bids at Wednesday's auction, dealers added.
